story.title: Churros a las nueve
story.teaser: Sunday morning in Madrid, the chocolatería is packed — so how does Grandpa know exactly when a table will be free?
lines: Es domingo en Madrid.
It's Sunday in Madrid.
— Abuelo, ¿vamos a la chocolatería San Ginés? —dice Nerea.
"Grandpa, shall we go to the Chocolatería San Ginés?" says Nerea.
A las nueve, hay mucha gente y no hay mesas libres.
At nine, there are a lot of people and there are no free tables.
— Podemos esperar —dice el abuelo—. A las nueve y media hay una mesa.
"We can wait," says Grandpa. "At half past nine there will be a table."
— Un chocolate con churros cuesta cinco euros —dice, sin mirar el menú.
"A chocolate with churros costs five euros," he says, without looking at the menu.
— Esos churros necesitan un minuto más.
"Those churros need one more minute."
— ¿Cómo lo sabes? —pregunta Nerea.
"How do you know?" asks Nerea.
A las nueve y media, hay una mesa libre.
At half past nine, there is a free table.
— Voy a la caja. Quiero pedir yo.
"I'm going to the till. I want to order myself."
— Dos chocolates con churros, por favor. ¿Cuánto es?
"Two chocolates with churros, please. How much is it?"
— Son diez euros.
"That's ten euros."
Un señor mayor sale de la cocina.
An old man comes out of the kitchen.
— ¡Fermín! ¡Cuarenta años aquí, y hoy eres cliente!
"Fermín! Forty years here, and today you're a customer!"
— Hoy no pagas. ¿Puedes hacer los churros, como antes?
"Today you don't pay. Can you make the churros, like before?"
— ¡Claro! Voy a la cocina.
"Of course! I'm going to the kitchen."
Nerea come y sonríe.
Nerea eats and smiles.
Son los churros del abuelo: los mejores de Madrid.
They're Grandpa's churros: the best in Madrid.
vocab: people (singular in Spanish: hay mucha gente)
without (sin + infinitive: sin mirar = without looking)

quiz.q: ¿Por qué Nerea y su abuelo esperan?
¿Cuánto pagan por dos chocolates con churros?
¿Por qué el abuelo sabe los precios sin mirar el menú?
options: Conoce muy bien la cocina de la chocolatería
Es el camarero de la caja

quiz.q: En la línea «Quiero pedir yo», ¿qué significa «pedir»?

story.prompt: Imagine you are at a café in Spain. What do you want to eat and drink, and how much is it? Write 3-4 sentences in the present tense with quiero, puedo or necesito and a price (for example: Quiero un chocolate con churros, por favor. ¿Cuánto es? Son cinco euros. A las diez voy a la caja.).

concepts.grammar: hay / no hay; querer, poder, necesitar + infinitive; ir a + place (voy a la caja, vamos a la chocolatería); time with a las; numbers and prices.
concepts.vocabulary: Café and ordering words: chocolatería, churros, menú, caja, pedir, pagar, ¿Cuánto es?
concepts.skills: Ordering food and asking for prices; following small clues to a surprise ending.

grammar.explain: 'Hay' = there is / there are; 'no hay' = there isn't / there aren't. It never changes for plural. Watch out: 'no' goes before hay ('no hay', never 'hay no'), and after 'no hay' Spanish usually drops the article: no hay mesas = there are no tables.
examples: Hay mucha gente y no hay mesas libres.
There are a lot of people and there are no free tables.
A las nueve y media, hay una mesa libre.
At half past nine, there is a free table.
—¿Hay churros? —Sí, hay.
"Are there any churros?" "Yes, there are."

grammar.explain: 'Querer' (to want), 'necesitar' (to need) and 'poder' (can) are followed by an infinitive: quiero pedir, podemos esperar. Only the first verb changes for the subject; the second stays in the infinitive. Querer and necesitar can also take a noun: necesitan un minuto. Watch out: querer and poder change their stem (quiero, puedes); necesitar is regular.
examples: Quiero desayunar churros con chocolate.
I want to have churros with chocolate for breakfast.
— Podemos esperar —dice el abuelo.
"We can wait," says Grandpa.
¿Puedes hacer los churros, como antes?
Can you make the churros, like before?
Esos churros necesitan un minuto más.
Those churros need one more minute.

grammar.explain: 'Voy' is the 'I' form of ir (to go): 'Voy a la caja' = I'm going to the till. 'Vamos' = we go / let's go. 'A' means 'to' before a place, and a + el = al (voy al café). Watch out: 'voy a + place' says where you go, but 'voy a + infinitive' says what you're going to do: voy a pedir.
examples: — Voy a la caja —dice Nerea.
"I'm going to the till," says Nerea.
— ¡Claro! Voy a la cocina.
"Of course! I'm going to the kitchen."
Abuelo, ¿vamos a la chocolatería?
Grandpa, shall we go to the chocolatería?

grammar.explain: Use 'a las + number' to say at what time something happens: a las nueve = at nine; a las nueve y media = at half past nine. For one o'clock, say 'a la una'. Ask with '¿A qué hora…?'. Watch out: 'Son las nueve' means 'It is nine'; 'A las nueve' means 'At nine'. Spanish never uses 'en' with clock times.
examples: A las nueve, llegan a la chocolatería.
At nine, they arrive at the chocolatería.
A las nueve y media, hay una mesa libre.
At half past nine, there is a free table.
—¿A qué hora desayunas? —A la una, el domingo.
"What time do you have breakfast?" "At one, on Sunday."

gq.q: Fill in the blank to say 'There are no free tables': ___ mesas libres.
gq.why: 'No hay' means 'there is/are not'. 'No' always comes before hay, and hay does not change for plural.

gq.q: Which sentence is correct for 'We can wait'?
gq.why: Poder changes its stem to 'pued-' only in some forms (puedo, puedes, puede); nosotros is 'podemos'. The second verb stays in the infinitive, with no 'a'.

gq.q: What does '— Voy a la caja —dice Nerea' mean?
options: "I'm going to the till," says Nerea.
"She's going to the till," says Nerea.
gq.why: 'Voy' is the 'I' form of ir (to go), and 'a' means 'to' before a place. 'I'm at the till' would be 'Estoy en la caja'.

gq.q: Which phrase means 'At half past nine'?
gq.why: 'A las + hour' says when something happens; add 'y media' for half past. 'Son las…' tells the time now, and Spanish never uses 'en' with clock times.

gq.q: Choose the correct word: En la chocolatería ___ mucha gente.
gq.why: To say that something exists (there is / there are), use 'hay'. 'Está' tells where a specific, known thing is: la chocolatería está en Madrid.

gq.q: Complete: Yo ___ pedir dos chocolates con churros.
gq.why: Querer changes e→ie in the stressed forms: yo quiero, tú quieres. 'Quero' does not exist in Spanish.

gq.q: Complete: El abuelo y yo ___ a la chocolatería.
gq.why: 'El abuelo y yo' = we (nosotros), so ir becomes 'vamos'. 'Voy' is only for 'yo'.

gq.q: Nerea and her grandfather arrive at nine. Which answer fits '¿A qué hora llegan?'
gq.why: A question with '¿A qué hora…?' is answered with 'a las + hour'. 'Son las nueve' only tells what time it is now.

steps.say: ¡Hola! Soy Nerea. Es domingo y estoy en Madrid con mi abuelo Fermín.
steps.en: Hi! I'm Nerea. It's Sunday and I'm in Madrid with my grandfather Fermín.
r: Hi, Nerea! What do you want for breakfast?

steps.say: Quiero desayunar churros con chocolate. Vamos a la chocolatería San Ginés. ¿Te gustan los churros?
steps.en: I want churros with chocolate for breakfast. We're going to the Chocolatería San Ginés. Do you like churros?
r: Yes, I like them a lot.
I don't know. What are they?

steps.say: Son muy ricos. Pero a las nueve hay mucha gente y no hay mesas libres. ¿Qué hacemos?
steps.en: They're very tasty. But at nine there are a lot of people and no free tables. What do we do?

steps.say: Mi abuelo dice: a las nueve y media hay una mesa. ¡Y es verdad! Voy a la caja. ¿Qué pido?
steps.en: My grandfather says: at half past nine there will be a table. And it's true! I'm going to the till. What do I order?
r: Dos chocolates con churros, por favor.
How much does a chocolate with churros cost?

steps.say: Un chocolate con churros cuesta cinco euros. Dos son diez euros. Pero un señor sale de la cocina y dice: ¡Fermín!
steps.en: A chocolate with churros costs five euros. Two are ten euros. But a man comes out of the kitchen and says: Fermín!
r: Does your grandfather work in the kitchen?

steps.say: ¡Sí! Mi abuelo conoce muy bien esa cocina: cuarenta años allí. Hoy no pagamos, y él hace los churros. ¡Son los mejores de Madrid!
steps.en: Yes! My grandfather knows that kitchen very well: forty years there. Today we don't pay, and he makes the churros. They're the best in Madrid!

culture.landmark: Chocolatería San Ginés, Pasadizo de San Ginés
culture.caption: Chocolatería San Ginés has served churros con chocolate in a narrow lane near the Puerta del Sol since 1894.
